attributes.description: Task 552 (milestone 109 item e), decisions 3166. Package opsdir-adapter-elastic, entry point elastic. naming (stream names, policy/template names, languages, kibana-space setting), lifecycle (ILM/component template/SLM documents and notes), detections (ES|QL wrap, rule bodies, notes), shipping (Elastic Agent action, container blocker), api and terraform (render targets), render (orchestrator), read (importers elastic/elasticsearch and elastic/kibana), collect (two collectors).
attributes.external_dependencies: ["Elasticsearch ILM, SLM, component template and data stream APIs (GET _ilm/policy, _slm/policy, _data_stream)", "Kibana detection engine API (/api/detection_engine/rules, _find, _import NDJSON)", "elastic/elasticstack Terraform provider (~> 0.16.6)", "Elastic Stack 8.x/9.x (current 9.5.5); ECS"]
attributes.purpose: SIEM add-on: the Elastic data streams an environment keeps logs in (stateful: ILM policy attached by the dataset's @custom component template, SLM snapshot archive; Serverless, ciamOffering serverless: each stream's data stream lifecycle), its detections as ES|QL detection rules, and the Fleet policies Elastic Agent ships the logs with (filestream per server log file, Kubernetes container logs by pod label), as API documents and Terraform for elastic/elasticstack; read back from the Elasticsearch and Kibana APIs (read-only collectors, API key) and its own documents (round trip).

attributes.description: Elastic Security as a SIEM: a siem-index destination whose reference is a logs data stream (logs-<dataset>-<namespace>) is kept by the Elastic add-on (stack role siem; its offering stateful by default, or serverless). Stateful: its searchable days render as an index lifecycle policy per stream (daily rollover, delete phase at the searchable days, none when kept indefinitely) attached through the dataset's @custom component template; days kept longer in all, with the archive's snapshot repository recorded, render as a daily snapshot policy expiring after the extra days, the delete phase waiting for its snapshot. Serverless: each stream's data stream lifecycle (data_retention the searchable days); an archive there is a blocker. Detections on a stream render as ES|QL rules counting matching events per window, every window of the rule's period breaching. Both as Elasticsearch/Kibana API documents and elasticstack Terraform, credentials only from environment variables. Read back from Elasticsearch (ILM or data stream lifecycle retention, effective retention first, snapshot archives, the build flavor against the declared offering) and Kibana (detection rules of any language), collected read-only with an API key. Named for the Elastic team: rule actions, when a policy or lifecycle takes effect, archives with no place, shared datasets, Serverless project retention limits. Shipping the logs is a separate flow.

How the products' logs reach an environment's Elastic data streams: the Fleet policies Elastic Agent is enrolled in, rendered from the log routes and the logs the products declare. Per server role an agent policy and per log file a Custom Logs (Filestream) integration policy: the file's glob under every install root, the stream's dataset and namespace, JSON lines decoded (ndjson; mixed files ignoring text lines), records spanning lines joined (multiline from the log's first-line pattern) and, when the routes take only some lines, the others dropped (a drop_event unless a kept-kind clause holds). Per role's container output a Kubernetes integration policy on the environment's Kubernetes agent policy, only its container logs stream enabled, its condition picking the role's pods by the deployment kits' label, the role's namespaces and the log's container. Both as Fleet API bodies (simplified format) and elasticstack Terraform (package install, agent and integration policies); package versions from estate settings. Named for the Elastic team: enrolling servers and running the DaemonSet (tokens never rendered), a catch-all Kubernetes policy duplicating, container lines shipped whole, a log two routes send to different streams (blocker). Not read back.

attributes.name: stack_component
attributes.purpose: Pure: a StackComponent record from a ciamStackComponent entry (role, adapter, accepted versions, source, its ciamRenderTarget values as targets, and its ciamOffering as offering).

attributes.name: lifecycle_notes
attributes.purpose: Render notes of environment m's data streams' retention. Stateful: none recorded (note), streams sharing a dataset (note when kept as long, else blocker), when each policy takes effect (action), an archive with no place recorded (action). Serverless (naming.serverless): none recorded (note), each lifecycle applying once the stream exists and the project's maximum retention (actions), kept indefinitely takes the project default (note), an archive Serverless can't keep (blocker; an archive ref with no extra days: action).

attributes.name: elastic_shipments
attributes.purpose: Pure: environment m's Shipments (core sources.shipments of its log routes and declared LogSources) whose destination is an Elastic data stream (naming.stream_name), on servers and on Kubernetes.

attributes.name: shipping_notes
attributes.purpose: Pure: the render notes of how environment m's logs reach its Elastic data streams: fleet.server_notes then kubernetes.container_notes (task 555; replaces task 552's Elastic Agent action and container blocker).

attributes.name: api_files
attributes.purpose: Render target api: {elastic/api/<file>: text} of environment m: its data streams' retention (ILM policies, component templates, SLM policies as GET answers; on Serverless data-stream-lifecycles.json), detection rules (NDJSON for _import) and the Fleet policies shipping its logs (fleet-agent-policies.json, fleet-package-policies.json: POST bodies, simplified format), each file only when it holds something.

attributes.name: terraform_files
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "m", "type": null, "required": true}, {"name": "notes", "type": null, "required": true}, {"name": "services", "type": null, "required": true}]
attributes.purpose: Render target terraform: {elastic/terraform/versions.tf, main.tf} of environment m (elasticstack ~> 0.16.6, credentials from environment variables; notes as comments, then the retention blocks (ILM, component template, SLM; on Serverless data stream lifecycles), detection rule blocks and the Fleet integration, agent policy and integration policy blocks); nothing when it renders none.

attributes.name: render_env
attributes.purpose: Adapter render_env: environment m's Elastic data streams' retention, detection rules and Fleet shipping policies in the render targets chosen (api, terraform), when it keeps logs in an Elastic data stream, runs a detection on one or ships logs to one.

attributes.name: parse_elasticsearch
attributes.purpose: (resources, notices) of one environment's Elasticsearch answers: logs data streams as siem-index destinations with searchable days (data stream lifecycle: effective_retention, else data_retention, else indefinite, also from the render's data-stream-lifecycles.json; else the ILM delete min_age of the stream's policy), days in all and archive repository from a covering SLM policy.

attributes.name: read_elasticsearch
attributes.purpose: Importer elastic/elasticsearch: the data streams' retention per <cloud>/<env>/ (layout_import of parse_elasticsearch, other SIEMs' notices left out), plus offering_notices when a cluster.json's build flavor disagrees with the stack's declared ciamOffering.

attributes.name: offering
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "m", "type": "EnvModel"}, {"name": "adapter", "type": "str", "description": "the adapter's registered name"}, {"name": "default", "type": "str", "description": "the adapter's default offering"}]
attributes.purpose: Pure: the offering of its product an environment's stack declares (ciamOffering) for the components a given adapter fills, or the default given when none records one.

attributes.name: first_streams
attributes.purpose: Pure: {(role, place, source path, source container): the stream the first of the Shipments given shipping that log of the role there ships it to}: the stream its Fleet policy reads it into.

attributes.name: shipped
attributes.purpose: Pure: the Shipments given that ship a log into the stream its first route ships it to (first_streams); the rest are clashes.

attributes.name: clashes
attributes.purpose: Pure: the Shipments given not shipped because their role's log already goes to another stream through its first route (first_streams), once per route and log.

attributes.name: clash_note
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "m", "type": "EnvModel"}, {"name": "x", "type": "Shipment"}, {"name": "first", "type": "dict", "description": "first_streams of the shipments"}, {"name": "what", "type": "str", "description": "the log in words (a file path, 'the containers output')"}]
attributes.purpose: Pure: the blocker RenderNote of a Shipment not shipped (clashes): its log (in words) already goes to the stream first_streams names, so the route's stream doesn't get it.

attributes.name: file_shipments
attributes.purpose: Pure: the FileShipments of the server Shipments given, a log file once per role, into the stream its first route ships it to: its globs under every install root, hosts, the routes' kinds and names.

attributes.name: parsers
attributes.purpose: Pure: the filestream parsers reading a LogSource's lines: a multiline pattern parser joining records from its line_start, then an ndjson parser decoding JSON lines into the event (add_error_key for json-lines, ignore_decoding_error for a mixed file); [] for plain text.

attributes.name: line_filter
attributes.purpose: Pure: the filestream processors keeping only the lines of a LogSource of the log kinds a route takes when it takes only some (sources.picks SOME): a drop_event whose condition is the negation of any kept clause (sources.kept_clauses: regexp ^prefix, has_fields, excluded rules negated; not-not collapsed); [] when all lines are taken.

attributes.name: agent_policy
attributes.purpose: Pure: a Fleet agent policy as POST /api/fleet/agent_policies takes it: id and name, namespace, description, the agents' logs and metrics monitored.

attributes.name: package_policy
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "name", "type": "str"}, {"name": "description", "type": "str"}, {"name": "namespace", "type": "str"}, {"name": "agent", "type": "str", "description": "the agent policy's id"}, {"name": "package", "type": "tuple[str, str]", "description": "(package name, version)"}, {"name": "inputs", "type": "dict", "description": "{input: {enabled, streams: {stream: {enabled, vars}}}}"}]
attributes.purpose: Pure: a Fleet integration policy as POST /api/fleet/package_policies?format=simplified takes it: id and name, description, namespace, policy_ids (its agent policy), package {name, version}, inputs.

attributes.name: file_policy
attributes.purpose: Pure: the Custom Logs (Filestream) integration policy of a FileShipment of environment m: paths, the stream's dataset and namespace, parsers and line filter as YAML strings, in its role's agent policy.

attributes.name: server_policies
attributes.purpose: Pure: (agent policies, integration policies) shipping environment m's log files on servers to its Elastic data streams: an agent policy per server role (namespace its first stream's), a filestream integration policy per role and file (package version from the elastic-filestream-version setting).

attributes.name: server_notes
attributes.purpose: Pure: the render notes of shipping environment m's server log files to Elastic: per role an action to enroll its servers in its agent policy (token and Fleet Server URL never rendered; the package to install first with the API documents), a blocker per file two routes ship to different streams.

attributes.name: container_shipments
attributes.purpose: Pure: environment m's container (on kubernetes) Shipments whose destination is an Elastic data stream.

attributes.name: container_condition
attributes.purpose: Pure: the Elastic Agent condition picking a container Shipment's lines: ${kubernetes.labels.opsdir.io/role} == role, ${kubernetes.namespace} in the role's namespaces (when recorded), and the container (== a sidecar's name, or != the role's other sources' containers); validated with Elastic Agent 9.5.5 in kind.

attributes.name: container_policies
attributes.purpose: Pure: (agent policies, integration policies) shipping environment m's container output to its Elastic data streams: the agent policy opsdir-<env>-kubernetes and a Kubernetes integration policy per role and log, container_logs alone enabled with its condition and the stream's dataset/namespace (package version from elastic-kubernetes-version); ((), ()) when none.

attributes.name: container_notes
attributes.purpose: Pure: the render notes of shipping environment m's container output to Elastic: an action to run Fleet's Elastic Agent DaemonSet on the clusters (and Elastic's catch-all policy duplicating), a note per route taking only some lines (shipped whole), a blocker per container output two routes ship to different streams.

attributes.name: data_stream_lifecycle
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "b", "type": "Entry", "description": "a ciamLogDestination naming a logs data stream"}]
attributes.purpose: Pure: (stream, its data stream lifecycle as GET _data_stream/<stream>/_lifecycle answers it and PUT takes it: enabled, data_retention <searchable days>d, none when kept indefinitely) of a data stream destination; None when it records no retention.

attributes.name: lifecycle_streams
attributes.purpose: Pure: environment m's kept data streams whose data stream lifecycle renders on Serverless: those recording a retention.

attributes.name: stream_parts
attributes.purpose: Pure: (type, dataset, namespace) of a logs data stream name (logs-<dataset>-<namespace>).

attributes.name: serverless
attributes.purpose: Pure: whether environment m's stack declares its Elastic component Elastic Cloud Serverless (ciamOffering serverless; default stateful).

attributes.name: fleet_name
attributes.purpose: Pure: the name and id of a Fleet policy rendered for environment m: opsdir-<cloud>-<env>-<part>-..., each part lowercased with runs of non-alphanumerics made a dash.

attributes.name: build_flavor
attributes.purpose: Pure: the build flavor GET / answers (version.build_flavor: serverless on Elastic Cloud Serverless, default otherwise), or None when the text isn't such an answer.

attributes.name: offering_notices
attributes.purpose: Pure: per <cloud>/<env>/cluster.json of an environment in record d, a notice when its build flavor (serverless or stateful) disagrees with the offering the environment's stack declares for Elastic (ciamOffering).

attributes.name: fleet_policies
attributes.purpose: Pure: (agent policies, integration policies) shipping environment m's logs to its Elastic data streams: the servers' log files' (fleet.server_policies), then the containers' output (kubernetes.container_policies).

attributes.name: data_stream_lifecycle_block
attributes.purpose: Pure: the elasticstack_elasticsearch_data_stream_lifecycle resource block of a data stream's lifecycle (name, enabled, data_retention).

attributes.name: integration_block
attributes.purpose: Pure: the elasticstack_fleet_integration resource block installing a Fleet integration package (name, version).

attributes.name: agent_policy_block
attributes.purpose: Pure: the elasticstack_fleet_agent_policy resource block of an agent policy body (policy_id, name, namespace, description, monitor_logs/monitor_metrics).

attributes.name: package_policy_block
attributes.purpose: Pure: the elasticstack_fleet_integration_policy resource block of an integration policy body: ids, namespace, description, references to its agent policy and package blocks, inputs as the provider's map with each stream's vars as jsonencode().

attributes.name: routes_named
attributes.purpose: Pure: the log routes a policy ships for, in words for its description: 'log route a', 'log routes a, b'.

attributes.description: One declared component of an environment's stack (a ciamStackComponent entry under ou=stack): the adapter, by registered name, that fills a role, the versions accepted, where to get it, the adapter's render targets the environment renders (ciamRenderTarget; () = the adapter's defaults) and the offering of its product filling the role (ciamOffering, the adapter's vocabulary; None = the adapter's default). A collections.namedtuple; targets defaults to (), offering to None.

attributes.description: One log file a server role ships to an Elastic data stream through a Fleet filestream integration policy: the role, its LogSource, the stream, its glob under every install root the role's servers record, the hosts, the log kinds the routes shipping it there take and their names. A collections.namedtuple.

attributes.description: Deferred notes 3185 and 3186 (worker). (1) Elastic Cloud Serverless has no ILM and no user SLM: a Serverless data stream needs the data stream lifecycle (template.lifecycle.data_retention or PUT _data_stream/<name>/_lifecycle; Terraform elasticstack_elasticsearch_data_stream_lifecycle). The reader already reads DSL retention. Needs a way to say a deployment is Serverless (estate setting vs record attribute: design decision, may change what the record holds -> escalate) and a decision on the archive there (no user snapshots). (2) Shipping to Elastic data streams isn't rendered (today an Elastic Agent action note; container output is a blocker): render Fleet agent and integration policies (elasticstack_fleet_agent_policy / elasticstack_fleet_integration_policy, a filestream input per file into the stream's dataset/namespace) and, if sound, Kubernetes collection. Research first via Codex (read-only): current Elastic docs for DSL on Serverless and stateful, Fleet agent/integration policy API and Terraform schemas, the Custom Logs / filestream input package, Kubernetes integration. Design to the master before coding. Showcase ids reserved: CHG-2100..2104, planted A240..A249, B100..B104.
attributes.name: Elastic Serverless retention and Fleet/Agent shipping
